answer: FINAL ANSWER (bixbench:bix-5-q1): Nervous system development (GO:0007399) — with an explicit caveat: formal GO over-representation could NOT be executed in this offline capsule, so this is the most defensible interpretation of the fully executed differential-expression evidence, not a computed ORA p-value. The executed DE analysis (median-of-ratios size factors + per-gene negative-binomial GLM, design ~condition+sex, Wald test, BH FDR, 42,883 genes tested) identified 658 differentially expressed genes at FDR<0.05 (427 up / 231 down; 544 with unambiguous HGNC symbols in the ORA universe). The disease fibroblast signature is dominated by neuronal-development and cell-adhesion genes — VANGL2 (padj 5.0e-94, the single strongest hit), CNTN4, CNTN6, SEMA4G, SEMA6B, ROBO3, LRFN1, CLSTN2, ADGRL1, GRID1, GNAO1, CHRM3, NEFH up-regulated; STMN2, PAX6, SCN1A, STXBP1, EPS8L2, CHRNA9 down-regulated — with no other coherent theme (neuronal/cell-adhesion keyword family 33/544 significant genes vs 22 glycosylation/metabolic, 26 chromatin/TF, 12 immune). If the gene-level DE set were subjected to GO BP over-representation analysis, nervous system development is the process the executed evidence points to as most enriched. GO ORA blocker (verified and documented in diagnostics.json): network unreachable (URLError to PyPI and Enrichr), no gseapy/goatools/mygene/pydeseq2/R installed, and no .gmt/.obo/GO annotation files anywhere on the system or in the inputs (gencode 'ont' column is empty; HGNC file has no GO columns). I did not fabricate annotations or an enrichment statistic.
